correctness.rationale: The proof classifies all nonempty factors by 1,2,3,4 maximal runs, accounts for duplicate 0-to-1 transition factors by rectangle intersection, and establishes a necessary and sufficient palindrome-pair criterion \(x=c\) or \(y=b\) for four-run factors. The exact count follows. Three exhaustive parameter cases (plus reversal-complement symmetry) bound the quadratic form, with positive explicit equality witnesses for all lengths at least eight. The standalone checker independently used direct factor sets and palindrome splits in 2500 comparisons, plus 1215415 exact-parameter tests; its finite checks do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The 2015 palindrome-pair richness question expressly proposes three-run maximizers. The first structurally adjacent class, four runs, is completely optimized for every length at least eight with a nontrivial exact coefficient and a linearly growing strict gap from explicit three-run witnesses. This rules out a major natural alternative family and yields an exact reusable run-shape factor-count identity; it does not rely on tiny gains, an arbitrary finite slice, or a claim of solving the global conjecture.
